summary: Join our Sustainable Finance Strategies and Principles Course to master the skills needed for responsible investing and sustainable financial practices.
lede: Sustainable finance integrates environmental, social and governance factors into financial analysis, investment decisions and capital structuring. For finance and sustainability professionals, this course covers assessing ESG materiality, analyzing climate risks through scenario analysis, and structuring green or sustainability-linked debt. It also includes hands-on practice with assessment tools, scenario models and sustainability disclosure drafting.
audienceIntro: This course is built for finance and sustainability professionals who are responsible for integrating ESG considerations into investment decisions, financial reporting, or capital structuring — and who need a structured, framework-grounded foundation to do it credibly.
modules: ESG Materiality Assessment and Double Materiality
Climate Risk Analysis and TCFD Application
ESG Integration in Investment Analysis and Portfolio Management
ESG Strategy, Reporting, and Stakeholder Communication
prerequisites: This course is designed for professionals at the foundation-to-intermediate level. No prior specialist ESG qualification is required. Participants should have a working familiarity with core financial concepts — such as capital markets, financial statements, and investment analysis — gained through at least one to two years of experience in a finance, treasury, risk, or corporate reporting role. No coding or programming skills are required. Participants who have previously encountered sustainability reporting terminology (GRI, TCFD, ESG ratings) will find the early modules consolidate and structure that knowledge; those encountering these frameworks for the first time will be fully supported through structured concept introductions before each applied exercise. Participants are encouraged to bring a current or recent sustainability report from their own organization to use as a reference point during disclosure mapping exercises.
